header.title: Install uv from the create venv from file notification, and the Allow Uv Python Install gate
header.result: Without uv, Yes on the requirements.txt or pyproject.toml notification and picking uv in Create Environment now ask to install uv, then build the venv. With Allow Uv Python Install off, uv is hidden or refused while it is missing. **With uv installed and Allow Uv Python Install off, Create Environment's uv option still lists and downloads Pythons that aren't installed.**
header.tested: the create venv notification (requirements.txt and pyproject.toml), Create Environment's uv option, uv install consent, decline, failure and retry, the setting off error and its link, the palette entry, and New Folder from Template's environment list
header.notExercised: the uv.lock notification, New Folder's Install uv button, and the Windows PowerShell installer

details.title: Change under test
details.body: The create venv from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml notification now offers uv whenever `python.allowUvPythonInstall` is on, and installs uv (with consent) when it is missing instead of failing. Create Environment's uv provider does the same. With the setting off, uv is left out of Create Environment while it is missing, `Python: Install Python via uv` is hidden, and any uv install is refused with an error that links to the setting.

details.title: State manipulation
details.body: Each scenario group ran in its own Positron instance launched for this run (four in all, on CDP ports 40783, 37799, 46133 and 38751, each stopped afterwards), with `HOME` pointed at an empty folder under the run directory and `/root/.local/bin` and `/root/.venv/bin` dropped from `PATH`, so uv read as not installed. The real uv installer wrote uv into that empty home. For the install failure, a `curl` stand-in that fails to resolve the host was put first on `PATH`, then deleted to remove the fault. `python.allowUvPythonInstall` was set through a seed settings file and through the Settings editor and user settings.json. Nothing outside the run directory was changed. The launcher's own CDP check uses curl, so it timed out for the instance with the failing curl, which was attached by hand. The pre-launched instance was not driven.

details.title: Branch verification
details.body: CI compiled `out/` in this job from the ref under test (head 9e0cbdf306). The behavior seen matches the diff: the notification says `Use uv` with uv missing, and the extension logged `Not installing uv: python.allowUvPythonInstall is off`, a line the diff adds.

details.title: Local noise
details.body: Every instance logged the same startup errors: extension manifests missing `engines`, a Copilot menu command not defined, GitHubLoginFailed, and an asyncio `client_connected_cb` error at each kernel start. None is tied to a check.

Press Escape to close the environment type list.

steps.observed: The list offers Python `3.14`, `3.13`, `3.12`, `3.11`, `3.10` and `3.9`, though only 3.14 and 3.12 are installed

steps.text: Pick the `Python` `3.11` row with the arrow keys and Enter.

steps.observed: uv downloads CPython 3.11.17 and a Python 3.11.17 (uv: ws-pyproj) console starts

findings.observed: With Allow Uv Python Install off, picking uv in Create Environment lists Python versions that are not installed, and picking `3.11` downloads CPython 3.11.17 and starts a console on it. A second try with `3.10` downloaded CPython 3.10.22 the same way.
findings.expected: With the setting off, Positron does not install Python with uv, as the setting's description now says: uv lists only the Pythons already on the machine, or is not offered.
findings.cause: The uv provider's version step ignores the setting and offers Pythons that uv would download. In detail, `pickPythonVersion` (`extensions/positron-python/src/client/pythonEnvironments/creation/provider/uvUtils.ts:40`) lists every version from `getUvPythonVersions()`, downloadable ones included, and `uv venv -p <version>` downloads a missing one. `getRankedProviders` (`extensions/positron-python/src/client/pythonEnvironments/creation/createEnvApi.ts:127`) keeps uv in the list whenever it is installed, and the PR's test `uv is still listed first when it is installed and python.allowUvPythonInstall is off` in `createEnvApi.unit.test.ts` asserts that. The version list predates the change, but the change rewrote the setting's description to promise that Positron does not install Python with uv when it is off, and gates uv entirely in the notification path (`autoCreateVenv.ts`) but not here.

cases.text: With `python.allowUvPythonInstall` off and uv installed, the uv provider's version step offers only installed Pythons, or does not create from a version uv would download.

verification.text:
A second agent re-read this report with the repository but without driving the app. Advisory only: no finding was changed or removed.

VERDICTS: 1=CONFIRMED

1. Matches the report's cause. `pickPythonVersion` in `uvUtils.ts` lists every version from `getUvPythonVersions()` with no check of `allowUvPythonInstall`. `uv venv -p 3.11` then downloads the missing Python, and the timestamps agree: the log shows `Selected Python version 3.11` at 17:21:46.381 and the download at 17:21:46.602. The environment setup (empty HOME, uv installed by the official installer) cannot explain a download that uv itself starts.
   - `createEnvApi.unit.test.ts` (new case `uv is still listed first when it is installed and python.allowUvPythonInstall is off`) asserts that uv stays listed when it is installed and the setting is off. That may be intended. It conflicts with the rewritten description, "Positron does not offer to install uv or to install Python with uv", so the reader decides.
   - `uvCreationProvider.unit.test.ts` has no case for the setting, as the report says.
   - Searches on "allowUvPythonInstall" and "uv download python setting off" turned up no matching issue.
   - The fix is in `uvUtils.ts`, which the diff does not touch, so I left it off the CHANGE line.

- The ledger's Noticed note O03 (the error notification's accessible name reads the raw markdown command URI) is plausible but was not checked, so I did not treat it as a defect.
- Linked issue #16192 is marked `fix held`, not observed, so the LINKED line is omitted.

No process issues.
